assertions.name: the two pn channels are exactly degenerate before any space index
assertions.source: mu+ * mu- vs mu- * mu+ -- commutativity, so equal identically

assertions.name: and no space FACTOR splits them, because both channels are S-wave
assertions.source: six values of g(L=0) applied to both channels alike; Lean separable_interface_degenerate covers every fSpace

assertions.name: the degenerate value reproduces qou-kj4v's recorded figure
mu+ + mu- = 1 -- the projector decomposition, so both channels bind
assertions.source: stated in qou-kj4v; unbinding needs mu > 1, outside the convex hull

caveats: Scope (b) for what it excludes -- a space index entering as a FACTOR -- with the invariant cited: commutativity plus a factor common to both channels. It does NOT close qou-vbyi. The Standard Model's tensor force is a spin-space COUPLING, and a product of a spin function and a space function is exactly what a coupling is not. A non-separable interface, depending jointly on (S, L), is untouched and remains the live shape.

Nothing here bears on 3S1-3D1 mixing itself, which is a genuine L = 0 vs L = 2 admixture WITHIN the deuteron. A space index is the right home for that; it is simply not what separates the deuteron from the virtual state, since both of those are S-wave.
The physics input -- that both pn channels are S-wave -- is quoted from qou-kj4v ('space symmetric'), not derived here. It is standard: 3S1 and 1S0 are both S in the term symbol.
